paragraphs: (a) Yuchasin omitted mention of him, apparently thinking Pappa and Pappi were one. It therefore gave R. Chanina bar Pappa's affairs under R. Chanina bar Pappi; this is not so. Eruvin 65a has R. Chanin bar Pappa, a scribal error.

(b) He distributed charity at night. The chief of the spirits encountered him and said, “Did our teacher not teach us thus: ‘Do not encroach on your neighbor's boundary’?” He answered, “Is it not written, ‘A gift in secret subdues anger’?” It fled before him: Jerusalem Talmud, end of Peah.

(c) The Angel of Death loved him and visited him regularly. They told the Angel of Death, “Go and do his will.” He appeared to him, and he said, “Leave me thirty days to review my learning, for happy is he who comes here with his learning in hand.” After thirty days he appeared. He said, “Show me my place.” He answered, “Very well.” He said, “Give me your knife, lest you frighten me.” He answered, “Do you wish to do to me as your colleague R. Yehoshua ben Levi did?” He said, “Bring a Torah scroll and see whether there is anything written in it that I have not fulfilled.” He answered, “Did you embrace sufferers of raatan, as R. Yehoshua ben Levi did?” Nevertheless, when he died, a pillar of fire separated him from the world. It is a received tradition that a pillar of fire separates only for one or two people in a generation. See Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak.

(d) R. Aleksandri approached and said, “Act for the honor of the sages.” It paid no heed. “Act for your father's honor.” It paid no heed. “Act for your own honor”—so they may approach you, eulogize you, and attend to you. The pillar withdrew: Ketubot 77b. He ruled that the bed be overturned for one day, and they showed him in a dream, “Because you rebelled”: Jerusalem Talmud, Megallechin, halakhah 5.

(e) Abba bar Marta; R. Abbahu; R. Yitzchak Nappacha; Rav Safra; Adda bar Avimi; Rav Acha bar Pappa, in his name. “R. Ila said: R. Chanina bar Pappa said.” R. Aleksandri; see above. R. Elazar. A teaching was recited before Zeiri [Terumot names R. Zeira]: end of chapter 5 of Shekalim; Terumot, chapter 7. R. Chama, his son. In R. Yochanan's name: Jerusalem Talmud, HaGozel UMaakhil. R. Yitzchak Nappacha; see above. R. Yirmeyah; R. Elazar; R. Shimon ben Lakish. R. Simon: Rabbah, introduction to Eikhah. Rav Safra; see above. He said: Rav Shila of Kefar Temarta expounded. R. Shimon ben Lakish; see above. He went up to R. Tanchum bar Chiyya: Jerusalem Talmud, Megallechin, halakhah 7.
